exposure: private midwifery care with hospital visiting rights
outcome: likelihood of having a first baby
newborn admission to Newborn Care Unit
cohort: The study audited 529 'all risk' women who received private midwifery care at one Queensland facility, with data compared to national core maternity variables.
finding: Women receiving private midwifery care with hospital visiting rights in Queensland experienced significantly better maternal and newborn outcomes, including higher rates of spontaneous labour and vaginal birth, lower rates of pharmacological pain relief, caesarean section, and newborn ICU admissions, compared to national averages.
mod_finding: The caesarean section rate was significantly lower (13% vs 32.8%) and the spontaneous vaginal birth rate was significantly higher (79% vs 54%) for women with a private midwife compared to national data.
